note: 18th accountability axis — Canadian Surface Combatant (CSC) procurement. LIRIL-advised through rounds 3 (surfaced under-reported), 4 (drafted PBO letter), 7 (fact-verified some claims 3/7, others near-correct). CSC is the largest single defence procurement in Canadian history, with Parliamentary Budget Officer cost estimates escalating from ~$26B (original 2014) to ~$77B (PBO 2021). This dossier captures Grover-markable actors with decision authority over CSC scope, schedule, or cost during 2010-2025.
primary_sources: Parliamentary Budget Officer 2021 report on CSC cost ($77.3B headline)
Parliamentary Budget Officer 2022 follow-up CSC cost report
Auditor General of Canada 2013 Fall Report Ch.3 (National Shipbuilding Procurement Strategy)
Auditor General of Canada 2017 Report 20 (Royal Canadian Navy Readiness)
Department of National Defence Strong Secure Engaged 2017 policy document
Public Services and Procurement Canada NSS public records

key_decision_points: 2010-10 National Shipbuilding Strategy announced (note: LIRIL R7 returned 2011; both dates appear in federal records — NSS selection was 2011, announcement October 2010)
2011-10 Irving Shipbuilding selected as combat package prime contractor
2018-10 BAE Systems Type 26 design selected (among three bidders)
2019-02 Lockheed Martin Canada confirmed as combat systems integrator
2021-02 PBO headline cost report $77.3 billion (LIRIL R7 returned $69.8B — close but not the PBO 2021 headline; possibly an earlier 2020 figure)
2024 ongoing contract amendments, first ship cut-steel schedule slippage
